jurisdiction.name: Equatorial Guinea
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Equatorial Guinea has no published AI-specific law, strategy or guidance identified so far. The government has created a State Secretariat for Artificial Intelligence and a directorate-general for AI systems within the ministry responsible for transport and telecommunications, but no founding text or AI policy document from them has been identified. Its only relevant framework appears to be a 2016 personal data protection law, whose official text is not online. A 2024 law on social networks, computer crime and cybercrime is published in full on the government's official website but contains no AI provisions.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation (State Secretariat for Artificial Intelligence)
narrative.review_notes: Not yet verified from the official text: the 2016 personal data protection law (Law 1/2016), the founding text of the State Secretariat for Artificial Intelligence and the ratification of the African Union Malabo Convention. Official sources checked on 18 October 2026 include the government's official website; still to check: the official gazette, parliament, the telecom regulator and the telecommunications ministry websites.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National government sources in Equatorial Guinea were searched, including the government's official website, the official gazette, parliament, ministries and regulators, and no qualifying AI-governance document was found in any category. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI material in the gazette or from parliament, the telecom regulator and the telecommunications ministry. The 2016 data protection law, the founding text of the State Secretariat for Artificial Intelligence and the Malabo Convention ratification are listed as leads.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. gacetaoficial.gq, ortel.gq, mtnt.gob.gq, camaradediputados.gq and senado.gq (guessed domains) proxy 502; guineaecuatorialpress.com reachable but its search returns nothing relevant. Guinea-Conakry AI roadmap results excluded. Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Searched, nothing found: no AI law or AI provisions found; official gazette and parliament sites unreachable. Data protection Law 1/2016 and a pending cybercrime/social-media bill held as leads (no official text online).; Government: Searched, nothing found: no national AI strategy, digital strategy with AI pillar, or public-sector AI guidance from the Government or the ministry responsible for telecommunications/digitalisation.; Ministries: Searched, nothing found: no AI documents from education, health, justice, defence, finance, labour or interior ministries.; Regulators: Searched, nothing found: ORTEL (telecom regulator) site unreachable; data protection body (Órgano Rector) reported not operational; no cyber agency or national standards body AI material; banking supervision is regional (BEAC/COBAC).. Not reached: Official gazette (Boletín Oficial del Estado) site unreachable; Cámara de los Diputados / Senado sites unreachable; ORTEL site unreachable; Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Digitalisation site unreachable. Could not verify: Ley 1/2016 de Protección de Datos Personales: no official online text; Status of the social networks and cyberspace (cybercrime) bill. binding-law, strategy, government-governance, ethics, risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found. Local retry 2026-10-18 (home connection, Saudi Arabia, about 20 minutes): www.guineaecuatorialpress.com (official government institutional site; gob.gq redirects there) opened via curl HTTP 200; its search form (POST /busqueda) works and was used for the queries listed. Still failing: gacetaoficial.gq, ortel.gq, ortel.org.gq, mtnt.gob.gq, camaradediputados.gq, senado.gq, presidencia.gq, guineaecuatorial.gq, inege.gq all DNS NXDOMAIN (curl and headless Edge) - these guessed domains appear not to exist; mintct.gob.gq resolves but returns HTTP 503 (curl and browser); inege.org HTTP 403; presidencia-ge.org HTTP 302 (not followed further). Findings: Ley Núm. 7/2024, de 23 de diciembre (social networks, computer crime and cybercrime) full text reproduced on the government site 2026-07-01 (Presidencia/Noticias); full text scanned: no AI/algorithm provisions, so out of scope (lead updated, not promoted). Government site articles (news, not sources) dated 2025-12-09 and 2026-07-04 name a Ministerio de Transportes, Telecomunicaciones y Sistemas de Inteligencia Artificial / ... y Aviación Civil, a Secretario de Estado de Inteligencia Artificial and a Director General de Sistemas de Inteligencia Artificial; no founding decree found. Article dated 2026-03-25 reports Chamber of Deputies approval of ratification of the AU Malabo Convention; no gazette act found. No official text of Ley 1/2016 found.

leads.title: Ley núm. 1/2016, de 22 de julio, de Protección de Datos Personales
leads.english_title: Law No. 1/2016 of 22 July on the Protection of Personal Data
leads.issuing_authority: Presidency of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea (promulgated law)
leads.note: General data protection law (data-privacy category); creates an Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales, reported by secondary sources as not yet operational. No official full text found online: the official gazette, parliament and telecom regulator (ORTEL) sites could not be reached and no official government host was found. Promote once an official text is located. Update 2026-10-18: the government's official website was searched again and no official text was found; the gazette, parliament and telecom regulator sites still could not be accessed.

leads.title: Proyecto de Ley de Regulación del Uso de las Redes Sociales y del Ciberespacio
leads.english_title: Bill regulating the use of social networks and cyberspace (cybercrime bill)
leads.issuing_authority: Cámara de los Diputados (Chamber of Deputies)
leads.note: Pending bill; parliamentary committee adopted articles defining computer crimes and cybercrimes in April 2024 (secondary reports only). No AI-specific provisions reported; final enactment not confirmed on any official source. Update 2026-10-18: enacted as Ley Núm. 7/2024, de fecha 23 de diciembre, por la que se Regula el Uso de las Redes Sociales, Delitos Informáticos y la Ciberdelincuencia; full text reproduced on the government's official website (published there on 1 July 2026). The text was read and contains no AI-specific provisions, so it stays outside scope. It provides for a national cybersecurity and critical-infrastructure body whose rules are to be set by regulation. Source: https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/ley_por_la_que_se_regula_el_uso_de_las_redes_sociales_los_delitos_informaticos_y_la_ciber_delincuencia

leads.title: Secretaría de Estado de Inteligencia Artificial / Dirección General de Sistemas de Inteligencia Artificial (founding instrument)
leads.english_title: State Secretariat for Artificial Intelligence and Directorate-General for Artificial Intelligence Systems (founding instrument)
leads.note: Government website articles of 9 December 2025 and 4 July 2026 name a Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence Systems (later named Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation), a Secretary of State for Artificial Intelligence and a Director-General of AI Systems. No founding decree or AI policy document from these bodies was found online (2026-10-18); the gazette could not be accessed. Would be a government-governance record once the decree text is found.

leads.title: Convención de la Unión Africana sobre Ciberseguridad y Protección de Datos de Carácter Personal (Convención de Malabo) - ratificación
leads.english_title: African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection (Malabo Convention) - ratification
leads.issuing_authority: Cámara de los Diputados (Chamber of Deputies)
leads.note: A government website article of 25 March 2026 reports that the Chamber of Deputies approved the proposal to ratify the Malabo Convention. No ratification act in the gazette or deposit record was found (2026-10-18). Regional data-protection treaty without AI-specific provisions; check against the regional AU file before any change.
